title: Sin que + subjuntivo: lo que no llegó a ocurrir

sections.content: Sin que + subjunctive describes an action happening while something else notably did not -- useful for narrating a missed opportunity, like two movements that shared an enemy but never quite managed to unite. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: El movimiento obrero no logró articularse con el movimiento campesino sin que existieran profundas diferencias culturales entre ambos grupos.
items.english: The labor movement failed to link up with the peasant movement, and profound cultural differences between the two groups were always present.

items.spanish: Estos sindicatos organizaron huelgas generales de gran escala, sin que estos movimientos consiguieran aliarse de manera duradera con las demandas campesinas.
items.english: These unions organized large-scale general strikes, without these movements managing to form a lasting alliance with peasant demands.

items.spanish: Esta separación no ocurrió sin que hubiera intentos genuinos de unirlos.
items.english: This split didn't happen without there being genuine attempts to unite them.

items.spanish: Ningún movimiento revolucionario logró triunfar de manera duradera sin que se produjera una alianza efectiva entre el descontento rural y el urbano.
items.english: No revolutionary movement managed to triumph lastingly without an effective alliance forming between rural and urban discontent.

sections.content: Sin que always signals two different subjects (the labor movement failed to unite... and profound differences existed); when the subject is the same for both actions, use sin + infinitive instead: se separaron sin resolver sus diferencias.
